questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Sri Lanka?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Sri Lanka on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sri Lanka article.

questions.proof: The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka is a tropical island nation located in the Indian Ocean just off the Southern coast of India.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Sri Lanka?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Ethnic make-up” part of the Sri Lanka article.

questions.proof: Their language is Sinhala which is an Indo-Aryan language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Sri Lanka shares a sea boundary with the _____ in the south-west and India in the north-west.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sri Lanka article.

questions.proof: Sri Lanka shares a sea boundary with the Maldives in the south-west and India in the north-west.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was known as Ceylon before _____, and Serendib and Sinhale, among other names, before that.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sri Lanka article.

questions.proof: It was known as Ceylon before 1972, and Serendib and Sinhale, among other names, before that.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Sri Lankan Civil War against Tamil separatists(LTTE) erupted in _____ and only came to an end in 2009.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Sri Lanka article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The Sri Lankan Civil War against Tamil separatists(LTTE) erupted in 1983 and only came to an end in 2009.
